note.text: The controller used a fixed reverse speed and only reacted to hitch angle later, allowing the trailer to swing left to ~15° and hit the rail. Head never turned to monitor side mirrors, missing the contact. Future drivers should keep the hitch angle small by steering toward the swing immediately, use side‑mirror looks or glance left/right to gauge rail clearance, and start with a lower reverse speed until the angle is under control. If the hitch angle exceeds about 10°, pull forward briefly to reset before continuing.

note.text: Got stuck pinned with trailer swinging about 76° right and ran out of time. The controller stayed reverse too long; it should switch to forward pull when the hitch angle exceeds roughly 70° or when status becomes PINNED. Prioritise early detection of a large swing and a quick gear change to forward, then steer to reduce the swing before resuming reverse. Tip: while reversing always steer toward the side the trailer is swung to.

note.text: The controller over‑steered right after each rear‑left touch, never reducing the hitch angle enough. Prioritize gentle steering within the 45° limit and switch to forward recovery earlier when the hitch drifts a few degrees. Keep the head aimed at the visible bay line to track swing and use the target bearing for small corrections. Remember only 8 touches are allowed, each adds a 5 s penalty, reverse speed is ~0.8 m/s, forward recovery ~1.2 m/s, and keep hitch below 7°.

note.text: Our controller used a simple proportional steer based on hitch angle, which kept the trailer swinging left and repeatedly bumped the left rail. The contacts caused gear‑change delays and ate the time budget. When the trailer becomes pinned, switch immediately to forward pulling to straighten before reversing again, and keep reverse speed low. Prioritize detecting PINNED status and adding a forward‑pull phase. Tip: watch the left rail with the head or mirror and only steer a few degrees left while reversing.
